comment: The Village of Lost Hours (SPEC 2026-09-26). Top-level world config; rooms/toons/things live in regions/, voice sheets in cast/, arcs in arcs/, stray minutes in minutes/, walkthroughs in walkthroughs/. Canon: docs/canon/LOST-HOURS.md. Assemble with: tools/assemble_world.py --source worlds/lost-hours

world.name: The Village of Lost Hours
world.aesthetic_seed: a small clockmaker's village at the bottom of a dream, at dusk; warm lantern-light on brass and old oak, moss in the seams of stone, paper lanterns, soft watercolor edges, the gentle mystery of lost hours drifting down like leaves

collect.name: stray minute
collect.seed: a stray minute: a tiny flicker of light no bigger than a moth's wing, turning slowly in the air as if it can't quite remember where it was going
collect.found_text: You cup the stray minute in your hands, and it settles: {name}. It was {text}. It slips into your Book of Stray Minutes.

dreamseed.name: dreamseed
dreamseed.seed: a seed like a tiny folded paper lantern, warm in the palm, with a light inside that beats as slow as a resting clock

growth.question: Where does the new way lead?
theme: a clockmaker's village at the bottom of a dream, at dusk
lost hours, kept and mended with patience
small rooms that hold one gentle purpose
quiet places where time can rest
growth.palette: warm lantern amber over deepening dusk blue; brass, old oak, moss-green; soft watercolor edges
motifs: moss in the seams of old stone
the hush between one tick and the next
things folded, kept, and labeled in a careful hand

exemplars.title: The Stair of Small Clocks
exemplars.seed: a narrow wooden stair where a small clock sits on every step, each ticking to its own slow count under a round window of dusk
exemplars.description: A small clock waits on every step, and no two agree on the time. Climbing feels like walking up through a gentle argument. At the top, a round window holds the dusk like a cup holds tea.

exemplars.title: The Room Where Letters Dry
exemplars.seed: a warm attic room strung with lines of pale ribbon, where rain-softened letters hang drying by a small iron stove
exemplars.description: Letters hang from ribbons like washing, drying slowly by the stove. Their ink has run a little in the rain, so every word looks as if it is still deciding what to say. The room smells of paper and warm iron.

exemplars.title: The Moth Library
exemplars.seed: a round library lit by one lantern, where soft grey moths rest on the spines of tiny books about the hours they once circled
exemplars.description: The shelves are no taller than a child, and every book is small enough to hold in one hand. Moths rest on the spines like bookmarks. When the lantern flickers they lift all at once, and settle again, each on the book it loves.

growth.husk_text: the spent, papery shell of a dreamseed, cool in the hand now, its slow light gone quiet; its dreaming is done, and the place around it is what the dreaming became

propagation.seed_text: a new dreamseed, paper-lantern thin and barely warm, its slow light only just learning to beat

growth.first_planting_text: Far off in the tower, the great clock gives one soft, deliberate tick. The dream has more room in it than it did a breath ago, and it was your hands that made the room. Down in the square, a lantern comes alight early, the way a house does when someone dear is coming home.

small-clock.name: small clock
small-clock.seed: a small resting clock no bigger than a teacup, brass gone soft with handling, its hands stopped at a quiet hour; by custom it is yours alone to wind

wind.description: Wind a clock. Target: the clock.

listen.description: Stop and listen to this place.
listen.fail_text: You listen. The dream is quiet here, in a friendly way.

sing.fail_text: You hum a few notes; the evening seems to lean in to listen.

variants: You stand still and listen. Somewhere a clock ticks, and somewhere else another answers it, not quite in time.
You listen. Far off, a lantern hisses softly as its wick settles, and a moth taps once against paper.
You listen to the village breathe: a door, a kettle, the long hush of moss growing in the seams of stone.
You listen, and for a moment you could swear the air itself is ticking, very slowly, like a sleeping clock.
